chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he said to Al-Hakam ibn Uteyba:

‘What is the time limit for pelting the Jamarah?’ So Al-Hakam said, ‘At the decline of the sun’. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: ‘What is your view if there were two men, so one of them says to his companion, ‘Guard our provisions for us until I return’, would he miss the pelting? By Allah, it is what is between the emergence of the sun and its setting’.

key_terms.رَمْيِ الْجِمَارِ: Pelting the Jamarah (stoning of the pillars)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct time limit for pelting the Jamarah during Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) refutes the restrictive view of Al-Hakam ibn Uteibah, establishing that the window for pelting the Jamarah during the days of Tashreeq extends from sunrise to sunset, not merely until midday. This ruling is derived through a practical analogy of a traveler leaving a companion to guard their goods, illustrating that the duty remains valid as long as the pilgrim is engaged in the ritual process. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining the flexibility of Hajj rituals and the validity of acts performed within the broader daylight hours.
